idiom_name: Seq/List of case classes via doobie .query[T].to[...] (JDBC underneath)
implementation_notes: Scala's idiomatic record set is an immutable collection of case classes: doobie is a pure-functional JDBC layer over java.sql whose high-level API maps each row to a type through a Read instance and materialises the whole set with .query[OrderRow].to[List]/to[Seq] inside a ConnectionIO (run with .transact(xa)); Slick's TableQuery results and Anorm row parsers do the same in their dialects, with java.sql.ResultSet as the bottom layer. What replaces the classic row/column container is the case class plus the collection - the column header is consumed once at the mapping site - and the ResultSet must never escape the transaction that owns it. Keep a generic tabular value (ResultSetMetaData, Vector[Map[String, Any]]) only for dynamic exports.
code_sketch:
case class OrderRow(id: Long, email: String)

val rows: List[OrderRow] =
  sql"select id, email from orders where total > $min"
    .query[OrderRow]
    .to[List]
    .transact(xa)
pitfalls: ConnectionIO/DBIO are descriptions: nothing executes until transact/run, and a java.sql.ResultSet captured outside the transaction is the classic closed-cursor bug - materialise (or stream via fs2) inside it.
Every row type needs a Read/Get (or a derived instance): a column-name or order mismatch fails at runtime, and nullable columns must be modelled as Option[T].
to[List]/to[Vector] materialises everything; large exports need streaming (doobie fs2 .stream, Slick streaming) or paging.
